thread.title: Dow Jumps 191 Points Because There's More to the Market Than the Midterms

title: Dow Jumps 191 Points Because There's More to the Market Than the Midterms
text:
Dow Jumps 191 Points Because There’s More to the Market Than the Midterms By Nov. 5, 2018 5:46 p.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
To the Polls. Monday was a mixed day for stocks , as the Dow closed up 191 points but the Nasdaq fell 0.4% under the weight of Apple’s tanking stock . All eyes are now focused on Tuesday’s midterm elections . In today’s After the Bell, we... ...explain why politics matters less for the market than other factors; ...say why EQT soared; ...and highlight Sysco’s market-leading tumble. Politics, Schmolitics
The U.S. midterm elections will be held tomorrow, but they’re likely more noise than signal for the market. The proof is in Monday’s market returns.
The major indexes ended mixed as the S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 2738.31, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 190.87 points, or 0.7%, to 25,461.70 but the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.4% to 7328.85.
There was a simple reason for that mixed market; two of them actually. They were Apple (AAPL),which continued to tumble following last week’s earnings report , and Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B), which rose after reporting earnings over the weekend ; Berkshire doesn’t trade on the Nasdaq. What does this have to do with the election? Nothing, and that’s the point. Companies matter. Stocks matter. Earnings matter. For the market, politics doesn’t matter, and I say that knowing that the Dow could tumble after the results come in.
But consider what’s been driving the market this year. Deutsche Bank’s Torsten Sløk highlight’s two opposing narratives. The bulls argue that economic and earnings growth are strong, and both will continue thanks to the tax cuts that kicked in this year, even if Treasury yields continue to rise. Bears, meanwhile, are contending that central banks are draining the world of excess liquidity, while the U.S. issues a ton of new Treasuries. Tighter financial conditions and higher Treasury yields will cause credit spreads to widen, and stocks to fall. Sløk believes the former will win out over the latter, though not without some bumps along the way. “The bottom line is that we see volatility higher, rates gradually higher, credit spreads gradually wider, and equities higher,” he says.
Notice anything about those two arguments? Neither depends on the outcome of the election. And ultimately, the election shouldn’t be what determines whether stocks go up or down. “[At] the federal level, this election’s legacy will be seen mostly in politics, not policy, so we see limited investment implications,” writes Justin Waring of UBS . “[Some] investors’ political fears overshadow their investment decisions, to often-disastrous results. Learning from their mistake, we have one recommendation: express your political views with a vote, not with a trade.”
Amen. The Hot Stock
EQT (EQT) shot to the top of the S&P 500, on a brighter outlook for natural gas .
EQT gained $2.72, or 8.3%, to $35.35.
EQT wasn’t the only natural-gas company gaining: Cabot Oil & Gas (COG) rose 5.9%, making it the day’s second biggest winner. Optimism stemmed from a rise in futures amid weather forecast calling for colder-than-average temperatures this month.
In addition, Morgan Stanley’s Mark Savino writes that tomorrow’s carbon-tax vote in Washington State “could be a pivotal catalyst for U.S. climate policy at the state level,” and “broader expansion of a carbon tax would be inherently positive for natural gas demand,” benefitting EQT and its peers.
Year to date, EQT is down 37.9%. —Teresa Rivas
Sysco (SYY) fell to the bottom of the index after reporting fiscal first-quarter earnings .
Sysco lost $6.73, or 9.4%, to $64.56.
The food-services company earned 91 cents a share on revenue of $15.22 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 92 cents on revenue of $15.39 billion. Sysco also warned that it continues “to see expense challenges in the warehouse and transportation areas of our supply chain, which we anticipate will persist.”
Year to date, Sysco is up 6.3%. —T.R.
